entry.name: itable
entry.description: Provides visual display of the table contents in your patcher window.

arguments.description: The argument gives a name to the. Max looks for a file of the same name to load. If two or moreorobjects share the same names, they also share the same values.

For example, for aobject with scripting name, the path of theparameter would be. You can set a value for thebefore the host object or parameter exists, and the object will connect to the parameter once it exists. Refer to the user guide entry forfor more details.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: The values stored in table can be entered and edited graphically with the mouse.

messages.name: bang
messages.description: In left inlet: Same as amessage with a random number between 0 and 32,768 as an argument.

messages.name: clear
messages.description: In left inlet: Sets all values in the table to 0.

messages.name: const
messages.digest: Fill the table with a number
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, stores that number at all addresses in the table.

messages.name: dump
messages.description: In left inlet: Sends all the numbers stored in the table out the left outlet in immediate succession, beginning with address 0.

messages.name: float
messages.description: Converted to.

messages.name: fquantile
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number between zero and one, multiplies the number by the sum of all the numbers in the table. Then, table sends out the address at which the sum of the all values up to that address is greater than or equal to the result.

messages.name: getbits
messages.digest: Get bit values from an index
messages.description: Gets the value of one or more specific bits of a number stored in the table, and sends that value out the left outlet. The first argument is the address to query; the second argument is the starting bit location in the number stored at that address (the bit locations are numbered 0 to 31, from the least significant bit to the most significant bit); and the third argument specifies how many bits to the right of the starting bit location should be sent out. The specified bits are sent out the outlet as a single decimal integer.

messages.name: goto
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, sets a pointer to the address specified by the number. The pointer is set at the beginning of the table initially.

messages.name: handtool
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, toggles setting theobject to use the hand tool. It is equivalent to setting theattribute.

messages.name: in1
messages.description: In right inlet: The number specifies a value to be stored in. The next address number received in the left inlet causes the value to be stored at that address.

messages.name: int
messages.description: In left inlet: The number specifies an address in the. The value stored at that address is sent out the left outlet. However, if a value has been received in the right inlet,stores that value in the specified address, rather than sending out a number.In right inlet: The number specifies a value to be stored in. The next address number received in the left inlet causes the value to be stored at that address.

messages.name: inv
messages.digest: Find the index of a value
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, finds the first value which is greater than or equal to that number, and sends the address of that value out the left outlet.

messages.name: linetool
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, toggles setting theobject to use the line tool. It is equivalent to setting theattribute.

messages.name: list
messages.digest: Store a value at an index
messages.description: In left inlet: The second number is stored in, at the address (index) specified by the first number.

messages.name: load
messages.digest: Fill a table with a stream of data
messages.description: In left inlet: Puts the object in load mode. In load mode, every number received in the left inlet gets stored in the table, beginning at address 0 and continuing until the table is filled (or until the table is taken out of load mode by amessage). If more numbers are received than will fit in the size of the table, excess numbers are ignored.

messages.name: next
messages.digest: Output value, then move the pointer
messages.description: In left inlet: Sends the value stored in the address pointed at by thepointer out the left outlet, then sets the pointer to the next address. If the pointer is currently at the last address in theobject, it wraps around to the first address.

messages.name: normal
messages.description: In left inlet: Undoes a priormessage; takes theobject out of load mode and reverts it to normal operation.

messages.name: penciltool
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, toggles setting theobject to use the pencil tool. It is equivalent to setting theattribute.

messages.name: prev
messages.digest: Output value, then move the pointer
messages.description: In left inlet: Causes the same output as the word, but the pointer is then decremented rather than incremented. If the pointer is currently at the first address in theobject, it wraps around to the last address.

messages.name: quantile
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, multiplies the number by the sum of all the numbers in theobject. This result is then divided by 2^15 (32,768). Then, table sends out the address at which the sum of all values up to that address is greater than or equal to the result.

messages.name: read
messages.digest: Read a data file from disk
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a name, opens and reads data values from a file in Text or Max binary format. Without an argument,opens a standard Open Document dialog for choosing a file to read values from. If the file contains valid data, the entire contents of the existing table are replaced with the data.

messages.name: refer
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by the name of another table, sets the receivingobject to read its data values from a namedobject.

messages.name: selecttool
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, toggles setting theobject to use the select tool. It is equivalent to setting theattribute.

messages.name: send
messages.digest: Send a value to a receive object
messages.description: The word, followed by the name of aobject, followed by an address number, sends the value stored at that address to allobjects with that name, without sending the value out theobject’s outlet.

messages.name: set
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a list of numbers, stores values in certain addresses. The first number after the wordspecifies an address. The next number is the value to be stored in that address, and each number after that is stored in a successive address.

messages.name: setbits
messages.digest: Change the bit values of an address
messages.description: In left inlet: Changes the value of one or more specific bits of a number stored in theobject. The wordis followed by four number arguments. The first argument is the address being referred to; the second argument is the starting bit location in the number stored at that address (the bit locations are numbered 0 to 31, from the least significant bit to the most significant bit); the third argument specifies how many bits to the right of the starting bit location should be modified, and the fourth argument is the value (stated in decimal or hexadecimal form) to which those bits should be set.For example, the messagewill look at address 47 in theobject, start at bit location 5 (the sixth bit from the right), and replace the 3 bits starting at that location with the bits 110 (the binary equivalent of the decimal integer 6). Suppose that address 47 of theobject stores the number 87. The binary form of 87 is 1111, so replacing the 3 bits starting at bit location 5 with 110 would change the number to 1111, which is the binary form of the decimal integer 119. The new number stored at address 47 in theobject will therefore be 119.

messages.name: sum
messages.digest: Output the sum of all values
messages.description: In left inlet: Sends the sum of all the values in theobject out the left outlet.

messages.name: write
messages.description: In left inlet: Opens a standard save file dialog for choosing a name to write data values from theobject. The file can be saved in Text or Max binary format.

inlets.digest: int Outputs Value at Index, list Stores Value
Sets Y Value for Next int at Left Inlet

outlets.digest: Outputs bang When Table Window Edited
